name: CT-RATE
description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices). Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report including impression and findings sections. Each volume is also annotated with 18 abnormalities. The dataset is used to develop CT-CLIP, a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework, and CT-CHAT, a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes.
creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Bjorn Menze, and collaborators from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, NIH, Imperial College London
publisher: Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital / University of Zurich
citeAs: Hamamci, I.E., Er, S., Wang, C., et al. Generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v5 [cs.CV] 8 Feb 2026.
rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. It includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. Each CT exam is accompanied by a radiology report authored by a radiologist, including impression and findings sections. The dataset captures substantial heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques. All chest CT volumes, associated metadata, and radiology text reports were anonymized before computational analysis.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Detailed metadata for the second external validation set (UPMC) is not publicly available, as it is a private dataset and cannot be shared. The RAD-ChestCT external validation set lacks a Mosaic attenuation label, which was excluded from external evaluation. The RAD-ChestCT dataset also lacks text reports, limiting report-to-volume retrieval evaluation to the internal validation set.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. Reports are structured into four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression. CT volumes were acquired using Philips (61.5%), Siemens (30.1%), and PNMS (8.4%) scanners.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API. Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and examined each report to remove residual personal information. CT volumes were anonymized by removing all identifying information from metadata. Volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Each chest CT volume's orientation was standardized by examining its metadata.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. CT volumes were then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480x480x240. Each CT volume was converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values were clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, values were normalized to a range of -1 to 1. For the RAD-ChestCT external dataset, identical preprocessing methods were applied as used with the CT-RATE cohort.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: To develop an automated label extractor model, 1,000 reports were manually annotated by merging findings and impression sections, identifying 18 abnormalities for multi-label classification. Conditions not referenced in either section were considered absent. Similar conditions were grouped (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; various lung opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules). The annotated reports were divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. The RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m model was finetuned on these annotations and then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports. For CT-CHAT training, a VQA dataset of over 2.7 million question-answer pairs was derived from CT-RATE reports using Llama 3.1 8B, including long-answer questions, short-answer questions, multiple-choice questions, and report generation tasks. Short-answer questions were derived using a rule-based approach. Text-only questions were generated from 48,343 PubMed Central OA articles related to chest CT.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Google Translate API (for translation); RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (for automated label extraction); Llama 3.1 8B (for VQA dataset generation)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned RadBERT model's precision, recall, and F1 scores were evaluated on a 200-report validation set, showing robust classification across all 18 abnormalities (F1 scores ranging from 0.95 to 1.00). For the VQA dataset generated by Llama 3.1 8B, only accurately generated and properly formatted data (parseable as JSON) was selected for training. For CT-CHAT evaluation, clinical accuracy was assessed using a Llama score (Llama 3.1 70B) and expert evaluation by three board-certified radiologists who independently rated 150 reports per model on a 0-10 scale.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: CT-RATE is publicly accessible via HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE). The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as future work. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are already included and openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face. Trained models and codebase are publicly available at https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP and https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CHAT.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (range 18-102 years, mean 48.8 years), sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male). All personal information was anonymized prior to release, including removal of patient and medical professional identifiers from reports and metadata.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CT-RATE addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging AI by providing the first large-scale open-source dataset pairing 3D chest CT volumes with radiology reports. This enables development of foundation models that can assist radiologists in diagnosing various abnormalities, reducing workload, and potentially saving lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The open-source release lays groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care.
rai:dataBiases: CT-RATE is a single-institution dataset from Istanbul Medipol University in Turkey, which may introduce geographic and clinical setting biases that limit generalizability to other populations. The dataset reflects a specific demographic (patients aged 18-102, 41.6% female, 58.4% male) and was acquired using scanners from only three manufacturers. CT-CLIP depends on the specific terminology used in reports, and variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy.
rai:dataLimitations: First, biases inherent to the single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training and limit generalizability to other populations. Second, CT-CLIP depends on specific terminology used in reports and the choice of prompts during zero-shot detection. Third, current models are limited to chest CT volumes and do not cover other 3D imaging modalities (MRI, PET) or other anatomical regions. Fourth, the quality of CT-CHAT generated reports remains insufficient for clinical use. Fifth, the absence of true 3D benchmarks for multimodal AI assistants limits comparative evaluation. The dataset does not include multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels (planned for future work).
rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and fine-tuning of AI models for: (1) multi-abnormality detection in chest CT volumes (18 abnormalities), (2) CT volume retrieval (volume-to-volume and report-to-volume), (3) radiology report generation, (4) visual question answering for 3D chest CT, (5) contrastive language-image pretraining for 3D medical imaging. The dataset supports zero-shot classification, supervised classification, and fine-tuning approaches. Not recommended for clinical deployment without further validation.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each CT volume is annotated with 18 abnormality labels. For the VQA dataset, over 2.7 million question-answer pairs are derived from the CT-RATE reports.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected Turkish-to-English translations of radiology reports. Three board-certified radiologists (two thoracic radiologists from Zurich and one from Istanbul) independently evaluated report generation quality.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned for automated abnormality label extraction from radiology reports); Google Translate API (Turkish to English translation); Llama 3.1 8B (VQA dataset generation); Llama 3.1 70B (clinical accuracy scoring); TotalSegmentator (organ-level anatomical segmentation labels); state-of-the-art 3D nodule segmentation algorithm (nodule information extraction)
